S1.name: S1 · SAP-hosted hybrid
S1.classification: SAP-hosted alternative for workloads where SAP coupling or verified platform economics justify this placement.
S1.objective: SAP BTP Cloud Foundry hosts and executes the agent. Apigee exposes the SAP MCP capability. AWS Agent Registry holds registration and discovery metadata only; no AgentCore component runs anything.
S1.ui_hosting: SAP Fiori launchpad or the existing application UI
S1.mcp_client: Inside the agent process on Cloud Foundry
S1.mcp_endpoint_type: Apigee-managed MCP endpoint (Pattern A); custom MCP server on Cloud Foundry behind Apigee only where logic needs code (Pattern B)
S1.mcp_gateway: Google Apigee (SAP-facing MCP/API gateway and runtime gateway)
S1.custom_mcp_runtime: SAP BTP Cloud Foundry, if required
S1.mcp_tool_execution_location: Pattern A: API operation behind Apigee. Pattern B: the custom MCP service on Cloud Foundry
S1.registry_publisher_approver: Integration team with the respective technical approvals; records published from the GitLab pipeline; AWS Agent Registry curator approves
S1.registry_sync: Records are published to AWS Agent Registry from the GitLab release pipeline through the registry API; synchronization from the endpoint URL only if Security approves AWS reaching it
S1.agent_discovery: AWS Agent Registry search, approved records only
S1.mcp_tool_discovery: Apigee MCP tools/list at the endpoint; endpoint metadata in AWS Agent Registry
S1.apigee_role: Required: the SAP-facing MCP endpoint and runtime gateway
S1.aws_account: Not used for execution. Registry records live in the central AI Foundry governance account
S1.llm_boundary: Cloud Foundry agent → Portkey → approved LLM provider. No direct provider route
S1.integration_suite: SAP Integration Suite (API Management / Cloud Integration)
S1.cloud_connector: SAP Cloud Connector, where the system connectivity model needs it (conditional)
S1.backend_authorization: Target SAP backend roles of the mapped user or service identity
S1.identity_boundary: Corporate IdP or SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS, candidate) → Cloud Foundry agent → Apigee → Integration Suite; token exchange and user mapping subject to validation
S1.persistence: Conditional: existing approved service, or SAP HANA Cloud where justified
S1.monitoring_audit: SAP BTP logs for the agent; Apigee analytics; Integration Suite monitoring; SAP change documents; registry publication audit
S1.artifact_repository: GitLab (central platform): source, specs, descriptors, CI/CD pipelines and artifacts; Cloud Foundry application artifacts; Apigee bundles
assumptions: Direct Apigee invocation from Cloud Foundry is approved by SAP Integration and Security
AWS Agent Registry can hold records for agents and MCP servers that run outside AWS
unverified: Actual Cloud Foundry consumption and contractual charges for frequent agent workloads
Scaling and capacity of Cloud Foundry for the workload
Supportability of custom orchestration on Cloud Foundry
Enterprise approval of direct Apigee invocation
policy_dependencies: Enterprise permits centrally registered but SAP-hosted agents
SAP Integration approves direct Apigee invocation
S1.hosting_note: SAP BTP executes; AWS Agent Registry only registers. Choosing the registry does not move the agent to AWS.
advantages: Closer alignment with SAP integration and BTP services
Reuse of existing BTP operating practices
considerations: Cloud Foundry consumption and contractual charges
Scaling and capacity for frequent agent workloads

S2.name: S2 · AWS AgentCore-native
S2.classification: AWS-native alternative, particularly suitable where AgentCore meets the technical and governance requirements without an additional Apigee gateway.
S2.objective: AWS owns agent execution, any custom MCP execution and the runtime gateway: AgentCore Runtime hosts the agent and eligible MCP servers, AgentCore Gateway mediates the tools, AWS Agent Registry registers them. Apigee is optional, only where SAP Integration and Security require it.
S2.ui_hosting: Existing application UI or SAP Fiori acting as an agent client
S2.mcp_client: Inside the agent process on AgentCore Runtime
S2.mcp_endpoint_type: AgentCore Gateway MCP endpoint to the agent; an AgentCore Runtime MCP server target, or an approved API/OpenAPI target that avoids a custom server
S2.mcp_gateway: AWS AgentCore Gateway (runtime gateway); Google Apigee only where SAP Integration policy requires it
S2.mcp_tool_execution_location: A custom MCP server on AgentCore Runtime, or an API operation behind an approved Gateway API target; the target must be validated before use
S2.registry_publisher_approver: Integration team with the respective technical approvals publishes; AWS Agent Registry curator (AI Foundry) approves
S2.registry_sync: Registry records created from agent and MCP descriptors by the GitLab pipeline; external sources via registry synchronization where supported
S2.agent_discovery: AWS Agent Registry search, approved records only
S2.mcp_tool_discovery: AgentCore Gateway tools/list (tool names prefixed with the target name); MCP descriptor in AWS Agent Registry
S2.apigee_role: Optional: inserted into the approved downstream route only where SAP Integration and Security require it; never bypassed silently
S2.aws_account: Dedicated SAP-agent AWS account (proposed, not provisioned); central registry in the AI Foundry governance account
S2.llm_boundary: AgentCore Runtime agent → Portkey → approved LLM provider. No direct provider route
S2.integration_suite: SAP Integration Suite (API Management / Cloud Integration)
S2.cloud_connector: SAP Cloud Connector, where the system connectivity model needs it (conditional)
S2.backend_authorization: Target SAP backend roles of the mapped user or service identity
S2.identity_boundary: Corporate IdP → AgentCore Runtime / AgentCore Identity → AgentCore Gateway → Integration Suite (or Apigee where inserted); token exchange and user mapping subject to validation
S2.monitoring_audit: AgentCore Runtime and Gateway observability; Integration Suite monitoring; SAP change documents; registry publication audit
S2.artifact_repository: GitLab (central platform): source, specs, descriptors, CI/CD pipelines and artifacts; the AgentCore runtime image, gateway target definitions and registry record definitions are deployed from GitLab
assumptions: An approved API/OpenAPI target or a custom MCP on AgentCore Runtime can reach the SAP Integration Suite API
SAP Integration and Security accept the route without Apigee, or approve Apigee as an exception
unverified: AgentCore Runtime, Gateway and Registry entitlements, quota and region in the dedicated account
API/OpenAPI target schema, authentication and connectivity to Integration Suite
SAP API policy exceptions if Apigee is omitted
policy_dependencies: SAP Integration policy on whether Apigee is mandatory for the SAP API route
AWS account approval and service availability
S2.hosting_note: AgentCore Runtime hosts, AgentCore Gateway mediates, AWS Agent Registry registers: three distinct capabilities. Apigee is optional, not assumed.
advantages: Centralized AWS runtime and tool-management capabilities
Less dependence on SAP BTP for general-purpose agent compute
Potentially simpler runtime architecture for AWS-native MCP capabilities
considerations: SAP API gateway policy exceptions if Apigee is omitted
AWS account permissions and service availability

S3.name: S3 · AWS AgentCore + Apigee hybrid
S3.status: Preferred candidate for a comparative POC · conditional
S3.classification: Preferred strategic investment candidate to evaluate first, conditional on account approval, identity validation, gateway interoperability, enterprise policy and measured comparative cost. Not production-approved.
S3.objective: AWS AgentCore Runtime executes the agent, AgentCore Gateway is the enterprise runtime gateway, and Google Apigee stays the SAP-facing MCP/API gateway in front of SAP Integration Suite. AWS Agent Registry registers agents and MCP endpoints on a separate control-plane path. A dedicated SAP-agent AWS account is proposed.
S3.ui_hosting: SAP Fiori or an enterprise application client
S3.mcp_client: Inside the agent process on AgentCore Runtime (framework executing in the runtime)
S3.mcp_endpoint_type: AgentCore Gateway MCP endpoint to the agent; Apigee-managed MCP endpoint (Pattern A) to SAP; custom MCP behind Apigee only where Apigee-managed MCP is insufficient (Pattern B)
S3.mcp_gateway: AWS AgentCore Gateway (enterprise runtime gateway) in front of Google Apigee (SAP-facing MCP/API gateway)
S3.custom_mcp_runtime: Conditional: an approved runtime, preferably AgentCore Runtime for AWS-owned code, exposed through Apigee
S3.mcp_tool_execution_location: Pattern A: API operation behind Apigee. Pattern B: the custom MCP service on its approved runtime, reached through Apigee
S3.registry_publisher_approver: Integration team with the respective technical approvals publishes from GitLab; AWS Agent Registry curator (AI Foundry) approves
S3.registry_sync: AgentCore agent record and Apigee MCP endpoint metadata are published to AWS Agent Registry as a control-plane path; gateway target configuration is a separate runtime responsibility
S3.agent_discovery: AWS Agent Registry search, approved records only
S3.mcp_tool_discovery: AgentCore Gateway tools/list toward the agent; Apigee tools/list behind it; the registry record is metadata only
S3.apigee_role: Required: the SAP-facing MCP endpoint behind AgentCore Gateway
S3.aws_account: Dedicated SAP-agent AWS account (proposed, not provisioned) with separate environments; the central registry may live in the AI Foundry governance account
S3.llm_boundary: AgentCore Runtime → Portkey → approved enterprise LLM. No direct provider route
S3.integration_suite: SAP Integration Suite (API Management / Cloud Integration)
S3.cloud_connector: SAP Cloud Connector, only for the applicable private-connectivity route (conditional)
S3.backend_authorization: Target SAP backend roles of the mapped user or service identity
S3.identity_boundary: Corporate IdP → AgentCore Runtime / AgentCore Identity → AgentCore Gateway → Apigee → Integration Suite → SAP backend; two token hops to validate
S3.monitoring_audit: AgentCore Runtime and Gateway observability; Apigee analytics; Integration Suite monitoring; SAP change documents; one correlation id joined across all of them
S3.artifact_repository: GitLab (central platform): source, specs, descriptors, CI/CD pipelines and artifacts; the AgentCore runtime image, gateway targets, Apigee bundles and registry record definitions are deployed from GitLab
assumptions: AgentCore Gateway can register the Apigee MCP endpoint as a target and exchange tokens
Apigee remains part of the approved SAP integration design
The dedicated AWS account is approved with the AgentCore services
unverified: AgentCore Gateway to Apigee: MCP protocol versions overlap (2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26) and outbound OAuth and token exchange are documented, but no end-to-end call has been made
Whether the Apigee endpoint is reachable from AWS (not yet checked)
Whether the registry credential provider is in the same AWS account (not yet checked)
Whether an external MCP server is an MCP or an HTTP target for the gateway; Apigee MCP does not support SSE streams
Non-duplicative responsibilities of the two gateways, quota ownership and tool naming
Dedicated account approval, quotas and region
Comparative cost against S1 and S2
policy_dependencies: AI Foundry and SAP Integration approve the gateway ownership boundaries
Enterprise approval of the additional gateway hop and its cost
S3.hosting_note: AgentCore Gateway fronts Apigee: two gateways in series with separate responsibilities. AWS Agent Registry is never an execution hop.
advantages: SAP-specific MCP/API governance retained through Apigee
Potential separation of compute cost from SAP BTP
considerations: Two runtime gateways need non-duplicative responsibilities
An additional network hop and gateway charges
MCP protocol and tool schema compatibility
Possible duplicated tool catalogs and policy controls
Multi-cloud incident management and audit correlation
Separate AWS account approval and operational ownership

evidence: Google Apigee
Apigee MCP overview
https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview

Existing Apigee APIs are exposed as MCP tools with no MCP server to install or manage. Stateless protocol 2026-07-28 and stateful 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05 at one endpoint over HTTP/S; SSE streams are not supported. OAuth 2.1 and OIDC. OpenAPI 3.0.x; 1000 tools per organization; capacity limits in some regions.
Pattern A needs no custom MCP server, within the limits. Apigee is not arbitrary agent-code hosting.
Tenant enablement, region capacity, hybrid version
Google Apigee
Manage MCP tool access
https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/manage-mcp-tool-access

Access is controlled with API products and developer apps; ParsePayload (JSON-RPC 2.0) plus API-key or OAuth verification; tools outside the client's product are removed from tools/list. This page says traffic can be proxied to your own MCP server.
Apigee is the SAP-domain policy layer. Pattern B rests on this one statement.
Prove the custom-server proxy pattern in this tenant
AWS AgentCore
Gateway core concepts
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-core-concepts.html
Gateway is a secure entry point for agentic traffic with MCP, HTTP and inference target categories and inbound OAuth (JWT), IAM, authenticate-only or none. It is not an agent-hosting service.
AgentCore Gateway mediates; AgentCore Runtime hosts.
Target classification of an external MCP server (listed under both MCP and HTTP targets)
AWS AgentCore
Gateway MCP server targets and outbound authorization
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-target-MCPservers.html

Supported MCP versions 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26. Outbound auth for MCP-server targets: none (not recommended), gateway role, OAuth client credentials, authorization code, token exchange, API key. Caller token passthrough is not supported; on-behalf-of is supported through token exchange. Listing mode DEFAULT when the server supports client credentials, otherwise DYNAMIC. Tool names are prefixed with the target name.
Four protocol versions are shared with Apigee. User identity reaches Apigee only through token exchange.
An authorization server that supports token exchange; private targets (not documented)
AWS AgentCore
AgentCore Policy
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/policy-getting-started.html

Cedar policies attach to a gateway; in enforce mode every tool call that reaches the gateway is evaluated and denied unless permitted. The pages do not say that a target blocks calls that bypass the gateway.
Policy is enforced at the gateway; bypass prevention is a separate credential or network control.
Prove that Apigee rejects a call that does not carry a gateway-issued credential
AWS AgentCore
Agent Registry
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/registry.html

A managed discovery service: a catalog for organizing, curating and discovering resources. Record types AGENT, MCP, SKILL, CUSTOM and WEB_BOT; publishers submit, curators approve. Runtime and Gateway are related services, so it is separate from both. The older preview namespace was announced for discontinuation on 2026-10-30.
The registry is a catalog, not a gateway and not a runtime. Use the agent-registry namespace.
Availability and region; cross-account sharing (not read in this build)
